Shallow-focus earthquakes are very widespread [1]. For example, they are found along
the Mid-Atlantic Ridge [1], the west coast of South America [1] and in much of southern
Europe [1].
Deep-focus earthquakes are much less common [1] and are found inland along the west
coast of South America [1] and in trenches, such as the Kuril, Philippine and Java Trenches
[1].
[Max 4 marks]

Shallow-focus earthquakes are generally located along divergent/constructive
boundaries [1] and along conservative/transform boundaries [1]. Deep-focus earthquakes
are associated with subduction zones [1], where one plate subducts beneath
another [1].                                                                                                                  [Max 4 marks]

Hazards associated with volcanoes include lava flows [1], which are slow-moving
‘rivers’ of lava that may reach temperatures of up to 800–1200°C [1]. Volcanoes also
produce pyroclastic flows [1], which are clouds of volcanic debris, cinders, ash, pumice
and gas [1] that travel at speeds of over 500 km/h and reach temperatures of up
to 700°C [1].                                                                                                                 [Max 4 marks]

People may live in areas at risk from volcanic activity as these areas produce fertile soils
[1] that are good for farming. These areas also attract tourists [1] and so create jobs [1].
Other advantages may include the creation of new land, mineral supply and geothermal
energy [1].
[Max 4 marks]

Answers should examine a range of impacts of earthquakes, for example ground shaking,
landslides, destruction of buildings, injury and loss of life, loss of economic activity, etc.
The impacts will depend on the magnitude of the event – stronger earthquakes will
release more energy than smaller ones. However, it is also important to assess the level of
development of the area affected; the depth of the earthquakes; the nature of the area,
whether it is rural versus urban; the population density; the nature of buildings; the time
of day or day of the week. In addition, there should be some assessment of attempts by
the government to manage the impacts of earthquake activity, such as through
earthquake drills, building codes, search and rescue teams. If the answer to this question
does not include examples, do not award more than 5 marks.
[Max 7 marks]
